title: Premium Accounting: The Driver Addition Charge on a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy
content:
The driver addition charge of a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy is the amount carried by the additional premium entry of a driver addition, for the term the addition falls in.

## Clause

The driver addition charge is computed as follows. Take the full-term charge of the addition. Multiply it by the operator share. Multiply the result by one plus the loss load percentage divided by 100. Multiply that by one less the loyalty credit percentage times its continuous-coverage share divided by 100. Finally, multiply by the charged days divided by the days of the addition's term. The product is rounded to the cent (half up) once, at the end, with no intermediate rounding.

## Terms of the clause

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Full-term charge of an addition | The full-term premium after the addition less the full-term premium before it, both as recorded on the addition entry |
| Days of the addition's term | Calendar days from the term effective date to the term expiration date of the term the addition falls in |
| Charged days | Calendar days from the date the driver addition was recorded to the term expiration date |
| Operator share | One |
| Loss load percentage | Nil |
| Loyalty credit percentage | Nil |
| Its continuous-coverage share | Nil |

The full-term premiums and the recorded date are read from the driver addition entry in the policy's transaction history. The term dates are read from the policy record.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

A driver addition entry shows 1200.00 before and 1650.00 after, recorded 1 March 2026. The term runs 1 January to 1 July 2026.

- Full-term charge: 1650.00 less 1200.00, which is 450.00.
- Days of the addition's term: 181. Charged days: 1 March to 1 July, which is 122.
- Charge: 450.00 times one, times one plus nil, times one less nil, times 122 divided by 181. That is 303.3149…, rounded once to 303.31.
